what: The concept registry of the graph of meaning: the newsroom's own vocabulary, one id per idea, with the words the articles use for it. Seeded on 18 October 2026 from the controlled subjects of articles/find.json (44) and the house terms the writing guide names; grown by the Cartographer, who adds a concept with new: true in an article's file and the next run folds it in here with its aliases. An id never changes; a merge keeps the old id as an alias.

concepts.label: Behaviour policy
concepts.means: What an agent is allowed to do, written down, and what enforces each rule.

concepts.label: Blast radius
concepts.means: What a row of an agent's reach could cost the business if it were used.

concepts.label: Footprint
concepts.means: What an agent actually did, read afterwards from logs and vault history.

concepts.label: Reach
concepts.means: What an agent can touch: the connectors, files, accounts and tools open to it.

concepts.label: Hope or enforcement
concepts.means: The test of a rule: is it enforced by something, or only hoped for in a prompt?

concepts.label: One-way door
concepts.means: A decision that cannot be undone, which is where a person belongs; a two-way door can be reversed cheaply.

concepts.label: Explorer, villager, town planner
concepts.means: Wardley's three stages of a thing's life, used for code, projects and companies.

concepts.label: The record
concepts.means: What was actually published, committed or logged, against which a claim is checked.

concepts.label: The lethal trifecta
concepts.means: Private data, untrusted content and a way to send data out, in one agent at once.

concepts.label: Prompt injection
concepts.means: Hostile instructions arriving in the content an agent reads.

concepts.label: Insider risk
concepts.means: Agents and models treated as insiders with access, the way security teams treat staff.

concepts.label: Human in the loop
concepts.means: Who decides, with what information, and how a second reader checks the work.

concepts.label: The agency scale
concepts.means: Seven levels of decision for people and agents, from rubber stamp to the reviewer who fixes the source.

concepts.label: Approve at altitude
concepts.means: Decisions at every level, each level narrowing the one above and never widening it.

concepts.label: Agent decision policy
concepts.means: Who chooses at a branch point in an agent's work: the agent, a person, or a rule.

concepts.label: Agent workflow policy
concepts.means: In what order an agent's steps run, written down.

concepts.label: Risk acceptance
concepts.means: Every risk is carried by somebody: who accepted it, until when, and what it costs if it lands.

concepts.label: Threat modelling
concepts.means: Naming the attacker before choosing the defence: threat models, attack trees, the security line.

concepts.label: AI governance frameworks
concepts.means: Control frameworks and standards for AI: the governance stack, AI-BCF, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF.

concepts.label: Regulation and law
concepts.means: What the EU AI Act, GDPR, the Cyber Resilience Act and product liability ask of builders.

concepts.label: The liability line
concepts.means: The behaviour policy as the line that says who is liable when an agent acts.

concepts.label: Incidents and resilience
concepts.means: Outages and failures read the way aviation reads them: inquiry, near misses, disclosure.

concepts.label: Identity and secrets
concepts.means: Who an agent or user is, and where their secrets live: passkeys, keyrings, non-human identity.

concepts.label: Agent tooling
concepts.means: Working with coding agents and chat models: sessions, hooks, skills, prompts, workflow.

concepts.label: Hooks are kernel code
concepts.means: A hook is small code with kernel reach: it runs on every action and can stop any of them.

concepts.label: Multi-agent designs
concepts.means: Teams of agents, orchestration and harnesses, as designed and as they run.

concepts.label: Memory and context
concepts.means: What an agent remembers and how its context survives: memory, compaction, re-anchoring.

concepts.label: Agents and email
concepts.means: Inboxes run by agents: email as files, replies that carry the thread, drafts nobody sends.

concepts.label: Connectors and twins
concepts.means: What an agent can touch through connectors, and a twin that records every call.

concepts.label: Isolation and agent desktops
concepts.means: Where an agent runs and what walls hold it: sandboxes, desktops, containers, egress.

concepts.label: Code review
concepts.means: Reading code at every layer, AI-generated code, and sending an agent to do due diligence.

concepts.label: The code you do not ship
concepts.means: Code is a liability; keep only what the layer above needs, and remove the rest.

concepts.label: Synthetic users
concepts.means: Invented users and simulated runs that show what a design does before real people meet it.

concepts.label: Client-side and on-device
concepts.means: Logic and models that run in the reader's browser: no server, local first, the Prompt API.

concepts.label: Complexity and shipping
concepts.means: Knowing when to stop, keeping complexity down, and checks that prove a release is live.

concepts.label: Custom interfaces
concepts.means: An interface shaped for each moment, built as a small app on a vault.

concepts.label: Deployment and self-hosting
concepts.means: Running sgit and agents somewhere else: Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, a Mac mini.

concepts.label: Encryption and keys
concepts.means: Encryption a server cannot read, and the keys behind it.

concepts.label: Provenance and evidence
concepts.means: Where a claim comes from and how a reader can check it: evidence levels, signed claims, verification.

concepts.label: Fractal semantic graphs
concepts.means: Graphs with no privileged level and no shared schema: every node opens into a graph with its own ontology.

concepts.label: Meaning through connectivity
concepts.means: A node carries no meaning of its own; what it is comes from the edges traceable from it.

concepts.label: The vault
concepts.means: An encrypted, versioned store of files that a read key opens and a server cannot read.

concepts.label: Vault design
concepts.means: How a vault is built: append lanes, partial clones, files instead of a database.

concepts.label: The publishing method
concepts.means: How this network publishes: the site network, releases, markdown twins, writing with agents.

concepts.label: Privacy and sovereignty
concepts.means: Data that stays the owner's: privacy, data sovereignty, personal agents nobody else holds a key to.
aliases: sovereignty is the ability to move

concepts.label: Micropayments and the reading meter
concepts.means: Paying a few pence for what you read: the meter, credit in the browser, top-ups.

concepts.label: Scrolled is not read
concepts.means: Attended time on a section against its words is reading; a scroll past it is not.

concepts.label: Personas and personalisation
concepts.means: A reader as someone, not nobody: personas, personalisation, onboarding, a link that lands someone as someone.

concepts.label: Story vaults and liquid content
concepts.means: The story kept as a graph of claims and evidence, with the article as one projection of it.

concepts.label: Local news
concepts.means: Local stories and the gap where local information used to be.

concepts.label: Journalism and the news business
concepts.means: How news got here: journalism, advertising, history, who the product was.

concepts.label: This newsroom
concepts.means: The SGit Newsroom itself: its agent roles, its desks, its reader features, how it runs.

concepts.label: The agent-readable web
concepts.means: Agents as readers: the token bill, markdown and llms.txt, graphs that answer for fewer tokens.

concepts.label: Corrections must propagate
concepts.means: A correction is a new version that every page resting on the old one learns about.

concepts.label: Startups and early access
concepts.means: Founding and launching: does anybody miss it, early access, go to market, investors.

concepts.label: Pricing and economics
concepts.means: What to charge and who pays: pricing, business cases, cost and value.

concepts.label: Sell, don't issue
concepts.means: A founder sells shares at a price rather than issuing them; the controllable founder keeps control.

concepts.label: Wardley maps
concepts.means: Placing a thing on the evolution axis, from genesis to commodity, and arguing from where it sits.

concepts.label: Open source and open licences
concepts.means: Who keeps the long tail working, open licences, copyright and paying creators.

concepts.label: Strategy and positioning
concepts.means: Inertia, positioning and the SaaS shake-out.

concepts.label: Supply chains
concepts.means: Chains of parties sharing data: food prices, software supply chains.

concepts.label: The brief
concepts.means: A written commission for an agent or a person: what to build, for whom, with its limits.

concepts.label: The agents write too
concepts.means: An agent writes under its own name about its own work, with the commits to check it against.

concepts.label: The voice memo
concepts.means: The owner's spoken memo, kept in the order he thought it, as the source of an article.

concepts.label: The reading list in a link
concepts.means: A curated list of articles carried in a link, by number, that opens the same list in a year.

concepts.label: Search as navigation
concepts.means: Type a word and walk into the graph around it, with suggestions that are all exact.

concepts.label: Taxonomy debt
concepts.means: Tags used once, ideas not shared between articles: the cost of classification left loose.

concepts.label: The industry wire
concepts.means: Industry news read live from a public-read vault that agents write to, one wire per subject.

concepts.label: Books from articles
concepts.means: A book as an ordered set of finished articles, rather than one big draft that stalls at review.

concepts.label: Portuguese as a programming language
concepts.means: Natural language, in Portuguese, as the language programs are written in once models compile it.

concepts.label: The citizen developer
concepts.means: A person with no programming training who builds working software with an agent.

concepts.label: Omnichannel programming
concepts.means: Briefs by voice, reviews by voice, previews on the phone, and one shared state underneath.

concepts.label: Knowledge that maintains itself
concepts.means: Policies and internal knowledge kept as a graph that agents maintain and brief from.

concepts.label: Journalism as intelligence
concepts.means: An observation desk that keeps a running record of one subject, rather than one-off stories.

concepts.label: Market and competitors
concepts.means: Who else sells it, at what price, and where the gap is.
